description: PCI DSS 4.0 compliance overlay — CHD tokenization, PAN redaction, and audit primitives for Stripe-backed commerce backends.

buildHints.whenToUse: Adding PCI DSS 4.0 primitives (CHD tokenization, PAN redaction) to a commerce backend. Reduces SAQ scope when paired with Stripe Checkout.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install && pnpm build` — tsc runs noEmit; zero errors means the scaffold is wired correctly.
Run `node validate-pci-pack.mjs` — prints 'pci-pack ok' when all required files and exports are present.
Wire `redactPanInObject()` from `src/pan-redact.ts` onto every log sink and error tracer before the SDK captures request bodies.
Use `assertNoChdInRef()` from `src/tokenize.ts` in every code path that accepts a payment reference object.
Import everything through `src/index.ts` — the barrel re-exports the full public surface.
gotchas: CVV must NEVER be stored post-authorization — PCI DSS 3.2.1 prohibits it even in encrypted form.
PAN in URL query strings is a violation — always POST to payment endpoints.
Test card numbers in fixtures (e.g. 4242…) still count as CHD in scope assessments. Quarantine test data.
Stripe restricted key: scope it to PaymentIntents only for server-side code; never ship the full secret key.
DO NOT log request/response bodies on payment endpoints without `redactPanInObject()` — log sinks ingest them unfiltered.
architectureNotes: Scope-reduction strategy: Stripe Elements handles the PAN client-side; the server only ever sees `pm_…` tokens.
CHD audit events must go to a separate log store from the general app audit log — commingling expands PCI scope.
The Luhn check in `redactPan()` prevents over-redacting random numeric IDs while still catching real PANs.

placeholders.description: PAN-redaction regex. Extend PAN_PATTERN for BINs your processor uses outside the standard Luhn range.
